newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Ortiz says peso not an inflation anchor.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Ortiz says peso not an inflation anchor.

text.p: Mexican Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz said Tuesday that the peso was not being used as an "anchor" to rein in inflation.

"It is not possible, we should not use the exchange rate as an anchor for inflation," Ortiz told legislators at the Mexican Congress. "We have to be careful that the exchange rate does not become overvalued."
But Ortiz said there were few economists who believed that the Mexican currency was currently overvalued.
"I haven't seen any analysis that (shows) that the exchange rate today is overvalued," Ortiz said.
He said the relative stability of the peso this year had been caused by an excessive depreciation last year and also by what he called an "important" entry of foreign capital.
He said what worried exporters was not the current level of the peso, but what could happen in the future if it remains "too stable" at a time of continued high inflation.
That, he said, caused many to fear that the "undervaluation margin" of the peso could shrink, thus hurting exports.

Referring to speculation that the government artificially sought to prop up the peso's value against the dollar in order to strengthen its fight against inflation, Ortiz said that such a strategy was out of the question under a flee-floating exchange rate regime.
Ortiz himself declined to comment on whether he thought the peso was under- or overvalued.
